extracted.intended_audience: patent lawyers, judges, and law students studying United States patent law (early 20th century)
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive treatise summarizing the doctrines, standards, procedures, and remedies in United States patent law (subjects of patentability, patent prosecution, claim construction, infringement, defenses, remedies, and practice). Intended as a practitioner's and student's reference covering statutory and decisional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Subjects of Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines what kinds of things may be patented (machines and improvements of machines; manufactures; compositions of matter; processes; designs) and distinctions among these classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes statutory/constitutional foundation; distinctions between 'process' and 'principle'; illustrations by leading cases (e.g., O'Reilly v. Morse, Tilghman v. Proctor, Telephone Cases); addresses ornament vs utility and designs under earlier statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention necessary to patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention (as opposed to mere skill or workmanship) is necessary for patentability; absence of a bright-line affirmative test but many negative rules to determine presence or absence of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates what is NOT invention (mere skill, excellence of workmanship, substitution of materials except in exceptions, enlargement or change of degree, aggregation, duplication, omission, substitution of equivalents generally, new combination without new mode of operation). Treats comparative utility and state of the prior art; invention questions are factual; joint vs sole invention; suggestions to inventors and information sought by inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is required for patentability; defined by absence of prior existence, knowledge, use, or prior printed publications that disclose the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers foreign knowledge/use, private foreign patents, prior printed publications and fullness thereof, abandoned applications, unpublished drawings/models, comparative dates, one instance of prior knowledge/use in the U.S. negates novelty, burden of proof considerations; novelty questions are factual. Special rules for designs, accidental prior productions, and antiquity of parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility (usefulness) is necessary to patentability; invention must have some function or useful result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility negatived by lack of function; perfection is not necessary; beauty may be utility for designs; functions that are evil or sometimes harmful may defeat utility; patents prima facie evidence of utility; doubts resolved against infringers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment (public use/on sale) bars
rubrics_metrics.description: Several species of abandonment can bar patentability including actual abandonment, constructive abandonment by public use or sale, and abandonment by laches pre- or post-application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'public use', 'experimental use', and 'on sale'; sale of an inchoate right; degree of identity required between publicly used/sold thing and patented thing; making/works/public knowledge do not necessarily constitute constructive abandonment; foreign public use/sale considered; rules described as inflexible; questions of abandonment are factual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constituents of patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Required components of an application: petition, preamble, general statement of the invention, description of drawings, detailed description, claims, signatures, oath/affirmation, fees, drawings, models, specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses particular requirements for machine, manufacture, composition, process, and design claims; form of oath and its constituents; Patent Office fees; dates of applications; registered Patent Office attorneys; examination, notification of rejection, appeals, amendments, when/how a candidate may amend, and interferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — form and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are the operative part of a patent; claims may be in varied forms depending on subject matter (machine, manufacture, composition, process, design). Particularity in descriptions and claims is a condition precedent to validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes claims in machine patents, methods of specifying parts, claims in manufactures/compositions/processes, design claims; generic vs specific claims; plurality of inventions in one patent; double patenting; particularity and sufficiency are factual questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of letters patent / claim construction principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be construed to determine their scope; construction involves legal rules and takes into account specification, drawings, application papers, contemporaneous statutes, prior art, and usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims construed in light of the descriptions and prior state of the art; functional claims, claims with reference letters/numerals; proper liberality vs proper strictness of construction; breadth governed by extent of use; construction in light of application papers and Patent Office limitations; questions of construction are issues of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularity and sufficiency of description
rubrics_metrics.description: The description (specification) must be sufficiently particular and full to support the claims and to enable skilled persons to carry out the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularity and sufficiency are conditions precedent to validity; sufficiency and particularity are questions of fact; claim language 'substantially as described' and how implied; deceitfully lacking or excessive specification and remedies and pleading in law and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and character of proof regarding novelty, utility, and invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation of burdens of proof and presumptions regarding patents' validity, novelty, and utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents and reissues are prima facie evidence of validity and utility; burden to overcome presumption described; patent questions (novelty, invention, sufficiency) often are factual inquiries; estoppel and admissions may affect burdens; specific sections discuss burden in novelty and utility contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimers — statutory authorization and proper use
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory authorization exists for filing disclaimers to correct errors in patents; disclaimers affect scope and ownership interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains errors that justify disclaimers (mistakes of fact relevant to novelty, mistakes of law relevant to invention), proper vs improper disclaimers, reissue claims, fraudulent or deceptive intention, effect of unreasonable delay in filing disclaimer, construction of a patent after disclaimer, disclaimers filed during litigation, and disclaimers required by judicial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissues — grounds and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue of a patent is available to correct defects (insufficiency, errors) but must comply with statutory and judicially imposed limits (same invention, no new matter, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: History of reissue statutes; subjects of reissue; definitions of 'specification', 'defective', 'insufficient'; faults justifying reissue; broadened and narrowed reissues; inadvertence, mistake and delay doctrines (e.g., Miller v. Brass Co.); same-invention requirement, new matter prohibition; reissues as construed liberally in some respects; reissues may be valid as to some claims and void as to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms and standards for extending the term of a patent: Congressional extensions and Patent Office extensions, statutory foundations, who may apply, and facts justifying an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mode of Congressional and Patent Office extensions, who may apply or benefit, timing of eligibility, force of Commissioner's decisions, proceedings preliminary to extensions, remedy for fraud in procuring/granting extensions, and scope of extension benefits to assignees/grantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title to patents — acquisition and transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: How title to patent rights is acquired and transferred (occupancy, assignment, grant, creditor's bill, bankruptcy, death) and the characteristics/effect of assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects of assignments, consideration, assignments of future inventions, assignments of accrued rights of action, recording and notice, warranties of title (no implied warranty of validity), reformation of assignments, equitable titles and their treatment, mortgages, trusts, and recording to protect against subsequent purchasers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses — scope, implied rights, and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Different forms of licenses (express to make/use/sell, implied licenses, oral/written), implied rights that flow with certain licenses, and limits on licensee rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express licenses to make/use/sell with implied leaves to use/sell as appropriate; licenses limited to particular purposes may not convey implied rights; implied licenses to repair/improve, from conduct, employment, or payment; recording and notice; clauses of forfeiture and effects; assignability of licenses; license restrictions on use and resale; warranty of validity of patent and of license; interplay with the Clayton Act and antitrust doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interfering patents and interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts between patents (interfering patents) and interferences between competing applications or patents — issues, evidence, remedies, and equitable relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics and causes of interfering patents; actions in equity between interfering patents; typical questions and evidence; injunctions and proper decrees; decisions in interferences not necessarily conclusive; appeals and practice before Patent Office and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal/invalidity for fraud or mistake
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds and procedures for setting aside or repealing patents obtained by fraud or granted by mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdiction in equity to repeal patents obtained by fraud or mistake, practice in such cases, and interplay with actions at law and equity remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qui tam actions under patent laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of qui tam suits within the patent law context — causes, parties, penalties, and forms of suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the wrongs that give rise to qui tam actions (e.g., fraudulent marking); the first two classes of wrongs and a third class; when illegal marking completes the wrong without subsequent use or sale; requisite form of declaration and forum; injunctions and appeals in qui tam patent cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for infringement — processes vs machines/manufactures
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for determining infringement for process patents and for machines/manufactures (including modes of operation and comparative results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by cases (Tilghman v. Proctor, Cochrane v. Deener, Mowry v. Whitney); addresses comparative results and comparative modes of operation; tests include sameness of function, substantial sameness of way of performance, addition/omission/transposition/substitution of equivalents, and change of form or proportion; knowledge of patent by alleged infringer is not necessary to infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of equivalents and equivalents in compositions/processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrine of equivalents applies to determine infringement when accused device/process does not literally practice all claim elements but performs substantially the same function in substantially the same way to obtain the same result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses equivalents in processes and machines, substitution of equivalents, primary and secondary inventions, necessity of change in equivalents, secondary patents, disclaimers of particular equivalents, substitution of ingredients in compositions (equivalent and non-equivalent ingredients), and cases such as Giant-Powder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for substantial identity and comparative utility as infringement criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative utility and substantial sameness (same function, same way) are used to assess whether an accused product/process infringes a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative utility may be decisive when other inquiries are insoluble; tests for sameness of function and substantial sameness of mode of operation described; examples and cases given (Ives v. Hamilton, Morey v. Lockwood, American Diamond Rock Boring Co. v. The Sullivan Machine Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement of design patents and compositions of matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for infringement when the patent is for designs or compositions rather than machines or processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses novelty and utility for designs; infringement of design patents by comparison of ornamental aspects; compositions of matter—substitution of ingredients, proportion changes, and equivalent/non-equivalent ingredients; disclaimers of particular equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for infringement — legal and equitable
rubrics_metrics.description: Available remedies include actions at law for damages, equitable relief such as injunctions and accounting for profits, and specific forms like preliminary and permanent injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses forms of actions, necessary allegations in declarations, damages (measure of profits, lost profits, royalties), accounting practice, equitable jurisdiction to enjoin infringement or repeal patents, interlocutory relief (temporary restraining orders, preliminary injunctions), stipulations, supplemental decrees, and effect of surrender/reissue on accrued damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of damages and royalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Various measures of damages for infringement (lost profits, reasonable royalties, accounting of infringer's profits) and treatment of royalties as a measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royalties as measures of damages for making, for making and using; established royalty rates' effect on preliminary injunctions; proportion considerations in measuring damages by royalties; reserve royalties on sale of patents are not dispositive; plaintiff's royalties do not cap recoverable profits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunction standard in patent cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Special presumptions and prerequisites are required to obtain a preliminary injunction in patent litigation, including some presumption of validity and adequate showing of likelihood of success and irreparable harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses the special presumption of validity needed, defendant admissions of validity as foundational, certainty of title required; effect of established royalty rate on preliminary relief; test cases may excuse delay; stay of accounting pending appeal, and standards for suspension of injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions at law — pleading requirements and defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper form and content of declarations in trespass on the case for patent infringement; required statements re novelty, utility, title, marking, reissue, disclaimer, extension, infringement, time of infringement, and damages. Twenty-eight defenses exist that may be pleaded in bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial (not merely technical) accuracy required; specific defences enumerated and discussed; special pleading rules and when notice of special matter required; general issue with statutory notice; many defenses require special pleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions in equity — practice and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Equitable remedies and procedure for patent disputes (bills for injunctions, accounting, cancellation, reformation), including jurisdictional aspects and appropriate decrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How repeals and equitable relief are pleaded and proven; practice on supplemental bills, bills of review; injunction forms and enforcement; masters' reports and exceptions; when equity will refuse or grant relief (estoppel, laches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and venue in patent litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Which courts have jurisdiction over patent cases (United States courts of first resort, limited state court roles, Court of Claims), and how venue is laid and qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-jurisdiction of state courts for patent validity/infringement suits; state courts may decide related contract controversies; jurisdiction of various federal courts described; venue rules for suits against aliens and other venue concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sue or be sued; standing and parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on which persons or entities may be plaintiffs or defendants in patent litigation: inventors, assignees, executors, administrators, owners in common, licensees (limitations), officers/directors/agents, joint infringers, contributory infringers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees cannot be nominal plaintiffs or sole nominal complainants; attorneys-in-fact cannot serve as nominal plaintiffs; who may be made defendants (minors, married women, employers, employees); causes of action based on plurality of patents or on patent and trademark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributory infringement and joint infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Liability rules for parties who cause or contribute to infringement and for multiple actors who jointly infringe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint and contributory infringement principles are outlined; partners, corporate officers, directors, and stockholders' liabilities discussed; statutory liability of officers/directors/stockholders and consolidated corporations as defendants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel, res judicata and admissions
rubrics_metrics.description: How estoppel and res judicata operate in patent cases; assignor estoppel and admissions by defendants affecting validity and relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Res judicata foundations and limits discussed; assignor estoppel to deny validity; admissions of validity as basis for preliminary injunction; estoppel by conduct, acquiescence, and litigation conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking, false marking, and qui tam penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing marking of patented articles, unauthorized/false marking penalties, and actions to restrain false marking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized marking punished and may be restrained; qui tam remedies for illegal marking; requirements to plead and prove false marking; vexing interactions with remedies and damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental use and shop rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental use may avoid constructive abandonment; shop rights may give employers implied non-exclusive rights to use employee-inventor's invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental use defined and delineated under abandonment doctrine; shop rights described as implied from employment and conduct; implied licenses from employment and payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use / on-sale bar and two-year rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Public use or sale more than two years before application can bar patentability under statute; what constitutes 'public use' and 'on sale' is delineated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed sections on what constitutes constructive abandonment by public use or sale; sale of inchoate rights; identification of timing (two years); foreign uses may be treated differently; exceptions for experimental use; standard cases cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution history and Patent Office procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Office examination, notification of rejection, appeals to boards/courts, amendments to applications, caveats, interferences, and actions to compel Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an applicant may/must amend, foundation of right to amend, how to amend, appeals within Patent Office and to courts, interferences procedure and appeals, and bills in equity to compel issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable accounting of profits and measure of infringer's gains
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounting for the infringer's profits is an equitable remedy and distinct from damages; the treatise describes when accounting is appropriate and how profits are computed and limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounting practice, relation to damages, role of trustees/infringers as constructive trustees, equitable decrees, and impact of surrender/reissue on accrued recoveries; precedents on profits as remedy discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial practice, masters, and appellate procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural guidance for trials (jury vs bench), masters' reports and exceptions, certificates and appeals to appellate courts and Supreme Court, and stays/supersedeas procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trials by jury and judge discussed; referees/masters practice, exceptions to masters' reports; appeals, writs of error, certificates to the Supreme Court, time for depositions, stays of accountings pending appeals, and practices on injunction appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent taxation and territorial scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights' interaction with taxation and territorial limits (territorial scope of U.S. patents and application aboard ships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents not subject to taxation in certain contexts; patented things may be taxed; territorial scope of U.S. patents (operation aboard ships, effect in ports) and treaties' impact on terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair vs reconstruction doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between lawful repair of a patented machine and unlawful reconstruction that amounts to making a new article (infringement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how far repairing is lawful, when a repair is unlawful due to license restrictions, and interplay with implied licenses and license restrictions on resale/use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for sufficiency of claim breadth and plurality of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on claiming multiple inventions in a single patent and on claim breadth; double patenting issues and when plural inventions may be improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plurality of inventions in one patent is addressed; double patenting doctrine; reissues and sub-combination claims; when sub-combinations may be properly claimed.
